rows.note: THE CALLERS FACTS PASS THROUGH UNCHANGED. The info block and the server URL are the mount's: @teamscala/service-boot titles the document for its own service and derives the server from the request Host and X-Forwarded-Proto, so re-deriving either here would be a second home for a fact the caller owns. The subject is the fixture wrapper because a row argument is JSON and an oRPC procedure carries valibot schemas, which have no JSON spelling (src/openapi-contract-fixture.ts says why); buildOpenApiDocument is reached through it in one call.

THE DEFAULTS, PINNED SO THEY CANNOT DRIFT INTO ABSENT: a caller supplying no options gets a titled document and a version rather than an undefined info block the mount would have to invent, and the servers member is a container with no entries. The two arg positions are placeholders and the subject declares no parameters, so the call takes neither: the registry writer renders a null arg as an empty string and collapses an array shorter than two elements (measured 2026-09-30 while filing this row), so absence is spelled as two empty strings rather than as the null the format defines. The servers list is asserted as an object member rather than as an empty array for the same reason.

STRUCTURE-DERIVED PATHS, THE CASE NOTHING ELSE COVERS. The generated CRUD routers declare NO .route() metadata, so the document path and method come from the router structure itself: /{namespace}/{procedure}, POST, operationId {namespace}.{procedure}. If derivation ever changed, every generated router on every portal would silently publish a document that does not match the routes it serves, and the live document would be the only place it showed. The fn namespace sits beside the model one so the separator is pinned for both shapes. Arg positions are placeholders; the subject declares no parameters (see the defaults row for the writer behaviour).

THE VALIBOT INPUT SCHEMA REACHES THE WIRE. A generated CRUD router declares its input as a valibot record, and this pins that the schema converter projects it as a JSON Schema object with string keys and open values under application/json — the fact that makes the document CONSUMABLE: a caller reads the accepted shape from the document instead of from the portal source. The valibot record spelling (type object, propertyNames string, additionalProperties {}) is the supplier conversion measured 2026-09-30; a supplier upgrade that changed it surfaces as this row going red, which is the point. The requestBody required flag is deliberately not pinned: the registry writer stringified it to a quoted true while filing (measured 2026-09-30), so a row could not state the boolean. Arg positions are placeholders; the subject declares no parameters.
